name: default
notes: The per-instance target. 1000 concurrent clients per app instance, a closed model where k6 VUs equal clients: 800 agents (400 read · 200 write · 120 claim · 80 run) and 200 signed-in readers (150 holding a Workbench tab · 50 browsing).

COMPUTED by the resolver — offered ≤ 824 req/s per instance (MCP 802 · /api/v1 12 · readers 10), so targetRps 500 sits under offered / 1.25 = 660. The busiest of the 6 agent workspaces is offered about 138 req/s, under 140 (70 % of the 200 req/s agent:workspace ceiling). Per credential the busiest agent offers 2 req/s (120/min) of the 600/min mcp:call budget, and a run token about 0.15 req/s (9/min) of the 60/min /api/v1 budget.
COMPUTED — 150 held streams + ceil(500 × 2 s) + 50 = a proxy hard_limit ≥ 1200 and a soft_limit ≥ 960 per instance, type requests.
ASSUMPTION — runs.agentSeconds 120 is how long a run VU's agent works before exiting. A shorter value raises the /api/v1 rate (requestsPerIteration grows by 2 per heartbeat beat plus the log events).
ASSUMPTION — readers.holdSeconds 300 is how long one tab holds its stream before reloading the page.
SHAPE — burst.size 189 is the 2026-10-13 move_to_parent burst (MOTIR-8259). Two burst agents per instance start 120 s into the steady window.

SHAPE — 6 agent workspaces per instance spread the agents under the per-workspace ceiling. 200 users, each a member of 2 workspaces with 4 tokens (one per role) in each, mint 400 agents per role, covering every role's VUs.
TIMING — ramp 3 min, steady 10 min (the requirement's at least 10 min after the ramp), ramp-down 30 s.
ASSUMPTION — roleSplit read 0.5 / write 0.25 / claim 0.15 / run 0.10 is the planner's decision for an agent-dominated mix (MOTIR-8678), not a reading of production traffic.
ASSUMPTION — toolWeights are chosen, not measured. transition_status carries weight 1 of 9 in the write role because each pick is TWO calls (todo → in_progress → todo).
ASSUMPTION — latencyAssumptionMs 200 (an MCP or /api/v1 call's p50) and readerLatencyAssumptionMs 300 (a page render's p50) feed only the offered-load arithmetic. The first smoke run reads both back.
ASSUMPTION — agentThinkSeconds 0.9 between a non-run agent's iterations, and readerBrowseThinkSeconds 5 between a browser's steps (±50 % jitter in the scenario).

COMPUTED — the offered load counts calls per iteration from the scenario code: read 1, write 1 + the transition share (1.11), claim 3 (claim, then release with update + transition, counted as always taking its card so the figure stays an upper bound). Run VUs come from requestsPerIteration. The burst and the per-frame workbench window reads are not in the steady figure.
ASSUMPTION — burst.retryAfterCapSeconds is the longest Retry-After any scenario waits before going on. It is the profile's only back-off cap, so every scenario receives it.
READING, NOT A THRESHOLD — proxy_shed (HTTP 503 per instance) is reported beside the verdict and judged by nothing.
